title: Hotfix: ignore out-of-order marketplace entitlement webhooks + backfill stuck activations
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Fixes a marketplace entitlement activation edge case where out-of-order webhook delivery could incorrectly downgrade an entitlement to INACTIVE, leaving orgs unentitled until manual intervention. Adds a backfill script to reconcile entitlements from raw webhook audit logs / upstream marketplace APIs.
description: Context: During AWS/GCP partner review we hit an activation edge case where entitlement webhooks were delivered out-of-order (retry + delayed delivery). Our ingestion path treated events as authoritative regardless of effective timestamp, so a late-arriving older event could overwrite a newer ACTIVE state (most commonly when AWS sent a REVOKED/EXPIRED update shortly after purchase retries, then the ACTIVE update landed first). Impact: customers could complete purchase but remain in `entitlement_state=inactive` in Redwood, leading to Console showing “No active marketplace entitlements” and blocking provisioning. This is a hotfix to make entitlement state updates monotonic by `effective_time` and to persist `last_applied_effective_time` per (provider, customer_id, entitlement_id). We now ignore out-of-order events and keep processing idempotent. Also includes a one-off backfill script to reconcile affected entitlements by replaying stored webhook audit events in timestamp order (and optionally validating against upstream GetEntitlements). Rollout: guarded behind `MARKETPLACE_ENTITLEMENT_OOO_GUARD` (default on in staging, off in prod until SRE flips). Adds metrics for ignored out-of-order events + backfill dry-run output. Notes: script is safe to run multiple times; it only updates rows when computed state differs and writes an audit log entry.
commits: marketplace: persist last_applied_effective_time and ignore older events
marketplace: fix idempotency to key on (provider,event_id) and store event effective_time
tests: add fixtures for out-of-order ACTIVE/REVOKED sequences
obs: counters for ignored_ooo_events and state_regressions_prevented
conversation: Ethan Park (author): Partner review found a real-world webhook ordering case that breaks activation. This PR makes state updates monotonic by effective_time + adds a backfill script for any entitlements that regressed. Scoped as hotfix; guarded behind a flag for prod rollout.
Cole Summers (reviewer): Can we confirm we’re not hiding legitimate revocations (i.e., an older effective_time but delivered later)?

Ethan Park (author): We only ignore events where `event.effective_time < entitlement.last_applied_effective_time`. If a revocation has a newer effective_time it will still apply even if delivered later. Added a test case for ACTIVE -> REVOKED with swapped delivery order.
Rafael Mendes (reviewer): Please add a metric for “state_regressions_prevented” and tag by provider. Also want a runbook entry for when we see spikes.

Ethan Park (author): Added `marketplace_entitlement_ooo_ignored_total{provider=...}` and `marketplace_entitlement_state_regressions_prevented_total{provider=...}`. Runbook: docs/internal/runbooks/marketplace-entitlement-backfill.md includes dashboards + thresholds and when to run the script.
Marcus Lin (reviewer): Backfill script calls upstream GetEntitlements—does it log any sensitive identifiers? Also ensure audit log entries don’t include raw payloads.

Ethan Park (author): Script defaults to replaying our stored audit-event table only; upstream validation is opt-in with `--validate-upstream`. Logging redacts customer identifiers (hash suffix only). Audit log writes only: provider, entitlement_id, old_state, new_state, and correlation_id; no raw payload.
Chloe Martin (reviewer): Console symptom is “No active marketplace entitlements” even when purchase succeeded. Does this fix that without requiring re-linking orgs?

Ethan Park (author): Yes. Org linking is unaffected; this only prevents state regression and repairs existing entitlement rows. Backfill will re-activate the entitlement record and Console will reflect it on refresh.
Cole Summers (reviewer): Migration adds last_applied_effective_time default NULL. How do we treat existing rows on first event post-deploy?
Ethan Park (author): If NULL, we apply the event and set it. Backfill script also sets it based on the newest applied effective_time after replay.
Rafael Mendes (reviewer): Looks good. Please coordinate rollout with ENG-4408 canary plan; flip the flag for 5% and watch ignored_ooo_events.
Ethan Park (author): Ack—will post in #eng-sre once deployed to prod canary.
Marcus Lin (reviewer): Approved with the redaction changes. धन्यवाद.
Ethan Park (author): Merging as squash. Follow-up: schedule backfill dry-run in prod and post results to incident channel; if deltas > 0, run apply with audit log trail.
